featured_reviews.name: Prateek Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
This stay was a classic game of "Good News, Bad News." If you’re looking for a room that’s spacious enough to stretch in but a bed that treats you like a piece of structural granite, you’ve found your home.
The "Good News" Suite: The room size was actually decent, the balcony was a lovely little extra, and the bathroom was clean enough to pass a white-glove test. Even the toiletries didn’t feel like they were made in a chemistry lab—total win.
The "Bad News" Bed: Unfortunately, the bedsheet felt like high-grit sandpaper, and the mattress was so hard I’m convinced it was just a decorated slab of concrete. On the bright side, the AC worked like a charm, so at least I was perfectly chilled while I contemplated my life choices on that "mattress."
The Hidden Tax: The "membership" and parking fees were a bit of a mood killer. It’s hard to stay motivated when you’re being nickel-and-dimed just to leave your car.
The Saving Grace: Breakfast was actually great! It was the exact "rebound" I needed after the night’s sleep-wrestling match.
The Verdict: It’s a bit of a mixed bag. Great vibes at breakfast, but your back might hold a grudge.

featured_reviews.name: Rutuja Yadav
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently stayed at this place and have good review to share!
This is at such a premium location in Colaba where all prime location are very nearby, almost walkable. The roads are clean and many heritage buildings nearby.

The hotel itself is very quiet and very clean. The service staff is very well trained and so welcoming.

They offer complimentary breakfast and dinner at certain time during morning and night respectively.

The menu is set but the food is very well made and almost tastes homely and not commercial. They offer breakfast with fruits, porridge or one Indian breakfast dish along with eggs as per your choice and toasts. They offer coffee and tea as well.

Dinner is served with one piping hot soup along with condiments such as pickle, yogurt and Indian dishes with roti and rice along with one veg and one non veg gravy dishes. Rice is also served with dal and salads with either combination of tomato, onion, cucumber or sprouts etc.
Dinner ends with a dessert or ice cream.
Both time during service the food is served with very well set tables, and attentive staff. The service of this place is rarely seen elsewhere as they all are cooperative , helpful and very well trained.

Not only the wait staff but the cleaning staff also does very good work with their work as the rooms are cleaned thoroughly and they pay much attention to the details.

The rooms themselves were small but very clean and nicely maintained with a wardrobe , tables and room service is provided every day.
They also offer laundry service if you require it.

We also asked them for a favor to keep some food items in fridge to be carried next day and they allowed it. Usually they said it’s not allowed but sometimes they can make an exception.

They also have parking space if you have your own vehicle.

Few complaints I have is the rooms may seem small for more than two people or with kids but the service does make up for it.

This is one of the hidden gem where you will have to spend so much money in the same area only to have shared bathrooms etc , but this is a very nice place to stay if you can get booking as most of the times it might be packed with Indian and foreign tourists alike.

featured_reviews.name: RISHABH
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is an outcome and vision of philanthropy and public spiritedness of old school business and something which we don't see nowadays. A hostel built on the ideals of women empowerment and social upliftment, this infrastructure allows a safe and secure residential accommodation in Mumbai for working women. The locality is not that great and safe to be precise and needs overhaul and immediate consideration by the local authorities. Although the locality of the hostel is a middle income area but the approach road and the adjacent place of the hostel is not safe for females because drunk local play cards and drink alcohol just outside the hostel although they are not an active threat, yet potential danger looms if your office working hours are late. The hostel is gated and manned by hostel staff and generally safe. The hostel has basic creature comfort and needs improvement, but are yet to get a filtered RO water purifier for the residents. Food served is not healthy at all and its nutritional value is poor the reason often given is the low price charged but the hostel is anyways a not for profit organisation and serving poor quality and quantity food in 2023 in a developing economy by a charitable institution run by one of India's largest corporate puts question on the overall management. Summarising the entire review, for potential residents they have a good place in Mumbai and it gives you a family safe place to grow financially in India's most expensive city at the same time the management needs to improve the infrastructure and use its CSR funds to overhaul and upgrade the hostel and make the residents feel like home, empowered and not that they are  at the mercy of some corporate magnate as it would be anthesis to the real value, philosophy and objectives of the Birla and ideals of Rajashreeji Birla.

I took this PG for one month, but unfortunately I had to leave within just 3 days due to serious issues.
Firstly, the PG is not organized or properly managed by the owner, Mansi. There is no hygiene maintained. The washroom and washbasin are extremely dirty and unclean. The kitchen is not properly accessible — only a few people are allowed to use it, while others are restricted. You cannot cook properly.
This is the month of Ramzan, and when I raised concerns regarding basic facilities, my complaints were ignored. The warden clearly refused washing clothes saying, “If I get time, I will do,” which is very unprofessional. There is also theft happening — many residents’ belongings are going missing.
Most importantly, there is no proper space or freedom to offer namaz peacefully. When I complained about these issues, the warden behaved rudely and misbehaved. After the owner Mansi leaves, arguments continue till 2 AM, disturbing everyone and that cause me a mental Harrasement.
The warden is a 19-year-old girl from Nepal who does not understand our language properly and is not capable of managing the PG responsibly.
There is a prepaid system — if you pay for one full month, there is strictly no refund under any circumstances. Even though the facilities and commitments promised on the first day were not fulfilled, they refused to consider any refund.
Because of all this, I lost my full amount of ₹6,000 within just 3 days.
Overall, it was a very stressful and disappointing experience. Basic hygiene, proper management, safety, and respect for residents are completely lacking.
